items.requestedAction: Document why shopping-intent lists belong to Base Commerce and what Profile owns.
items.rationale: The guide directly answers the requested boundary: wishlists, compare and save-for-later carry product/SKU/store shopping intent and belong to Base Commerce; Profile owns customer identity, authentication and enterprise access rather than a second list store. It explains stable owner/tenant keys, explicit store context, Commerce permission ownership, migration without dual authority and customer-safe service access. The current source enforces owner-scoped routes and operations. The pass is for that exact ownership request, not a blanket endorsement of every customization example in the article. Final source-citation rereview: the Profile group source formerly named in the guide is absent. Current owner init-v001/records/identity/profileUserGroupData.js contains commerce.shoppingList.own in the genuine customerUserGroup. Replaced only that citation and its source-map table cell in a new 0.0.2/docs-v002 successor. Exact structured comparison proves all other blocks, headings, routes and source evidence unchanged; all previously reviewed controller/service/router hashes still match. Profile remains permission authority, Shopping List remains shopping-intent owner, and no installed groups or permissions changed. Prior bounded customization limitation remains explicit.
sourceFindings: Customer routes require commerce.shoppingList.own and the owning customer controller, not generic Profile CRUD.
Operation queries scope lists and entries by tenant and owner, list type and explicit store context; list policy remains a Commerce concern.
limit handles COMPARE and SAVE_FOR_LATER specially; all other types use maximumWishlistItems.
correctnessAndCoverageLimitations: Nonblocking to the requested ownership explanation: the extra outfit/gift customization example suggests per-type maximumOutfitIdeaItems/maximumGiftIdeaItems settings. limit does not consume those keys. Correct that example or explain the required operation-service override; setting those properties alone does not enforce those limits.

liveAcceptance.boundary: Browser, deployed-runtime and live-provider acceptance were not executed; this source editorial disposition neither grants nor denies those separate gates.
